source.title: From Concepts to Actual Causes: Toward Closing the Concept-Malfunction Gap in Robot Foundation Models

page_placements.theme: Compensation and downstream erasure also distort non-ablation attribution, and blocking compensation changes rankings

record.file_problem: none noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses backup effects and cites the Hydra effect, but it reports no results on language-model ablations or the claim versions. Its own example is a toy robot policy.
record.gate_note: The toy example reports intervention outcomes that illustrate component backups in a robot policy; they are recorded under fits_no_version because they do not test the language-model behaviors specified by the versions. The probing and visual-attribution observations concern concepts or input masking, not the claimed language-model ablation behavior. The paper explicitly says it has no experiments on real RFMs.
record.test_reason: A position paper that cites the Hydra effect to motivate its idea of 'contingencies' for backup components. Its only results come from a hand-built toy robot policy with an analytic acceleration law and a designed backup drive g. It runs no trained language model and no ablation of attention layers, heads or MLPs, and it measures no emergent compensation. None of its results bear on any version. Its argument that fixed-contingency methods miss backed-up causes resembles V7 in spirit. That argument rests only on a designed toy, so it is not a test of V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The authors argue that MI fault-isolation queries are misspecified because they use fixed contingencies, single-step interventions, unrealizable counterfactuals and immediate read-outs. This lets backups obscure actual causes. The toy example is illustrative only, and empirical validation on real RFMs is left to future work.
record.recipe_differences: No language-model ablation method was run; the paper gives a formal framework and a toy robot-policy example.
record.method_sensitivity: In the toy example, the result differs between a single-step readout, patching across steps with the backup free to respond, and patching with the backup frozen.

fits_no_version.finding: In a hand-designed toy robot policy, single-step patching of the suppressor gives an immediate braking effect (|Δa0| = 2 m/s²). The breach still occurs, 0.1 s later. Patching at all steps lets the backup drive g restore speed (breach at 3.3 s). Freezing g averts the breach (1.8 m clear).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In closed-loop policies, a designed backup component can mask a component's causal role: immediate-effect or fixed-contingency interventions misattribute the cause, while searching contingencies recovers it.

record.problems: No experiments on real RFMs; the argument relies on a toy example and assumes a faithful deterministic simulator. No uncertainty estimates or empirical controls are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant intervention outcomes were left out. Observations about probing and visual attribution concern concept identification or input masking rather than the specified language-model ablation behaviors.

untested.parts: No attention-layer ablation or downstream compensation in any language model.
No MLP output or maximum-likelihood-token erasure measured.
No head ablations or general-text results.
No measurement of how much compensation occurs, how it varies by prompt, or whether it overcorrects.
No named repair mechanisms (backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling, anti-erasure neurons) examined.
No comparison of mean, resample and zero ablation.
No ablation-based importance scores computed on a trained model. The toy's backup is designed in, not emergent.

record.verdict_notes: The record's rows, relation and tranche are accurate. All rows correctly link to 'none' with state cannot_determine. The 'backup' g is hand-coded into an analytic policy, not compensation that emerges in a trained network. The Hydra effect is cited only as motivation. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No language-model attention-layer ablation or later-layer compensation tested.
No late-MLP output or maximum-likelihood-token erasure measured.
No attention-head ablations or full-distribution results on general text tested.
No prompt-level variability or overcorrection in language-model self-repair measured.
No named language-model repair mechanisms tested.
No ablation-based language-model importance scores evaluated.

relation.reason: Section 2 cites the Hydra effect as an example of backup components obscuring but-for causation; the paper does not test language-model self-repair.

tranche.reason: The hand-designed toy policy illustrates causal-query misspecification; it tests none of the claim versions about self-repair in trained language models.
